Commentary on Surah "Al-'Asr" (The Declining Day). It is Meccan, though Qatadah said it is Medinan, and this is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas. It has three verses. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By time,﴾ (1)

On this verse there are two issues.

The first: the statement of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿By time (al-'asr)﴾, meaning by the age (al-dahr). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and others. So al-'asr is like al-dahr, and from this is the saying of the poet:

The path of passion is rough, and the sea of passion is deep... and the day of passion is a month, and the month of passion is an age.

That is, an age by which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, swears, because of what it contains of admonition through the changing of circumstances and their transformation, and of the indication it provides of the Creator. It has also been said: al-'asr is the night and the day. Humayd ibn Thawr said:

And the two 'asrs will not delay, a day and a night, when they seek to overtake whatever they aim at.

Al-'asrani also means the morning and the evening. He said:

I postpone him over the two 'asrs until he tires of me, and he accepts half the debt while his nose is humbled.

He means: when he comes to me at the beginning of the day, I promise him its end. It has also been said that it is the evening (al-'ashiy), which is the period between the decline of the sun and its setting, said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. From this is the saying of the poet:

Let us go out in the afternoon, O 'Amr, for the 'asr has grown short, and in the first going out is the spoil and the reward.

It is also reported from Qatadah: it is the last hour of the hours of the day. It has also been said: it is an oath by the prayer of 'Asr, which is the middle prayer (al-wusta), because it is the most excellent of the prayers, said by Muqatil. It is said: "Adhdhin lil-'asr," meaning for the prayer of 'Asr, and "Sallaytu al-'asr," meaning the prayer of 'Asr. In the sound report: [The middle prayer is the prayer of 'Asr]. Its explanation has already passed in Surah al-Baqarah [[see vol. 3 p. 210]]. It has also been said: it is an oath by the era of the Prophet (ﷺ), because of its excellence through the renewal of prophethood in it. It has also been said: its meaning is "by the Lord of the 'asr."

The second: Malik said: whoever swears that he will not speak to a man for an 'asr, he will not speak to him for a year. Ibn al-'Arabi said: "Malik only interpreted the oath of one who swears not to speak to a person for an 'asr as a year, because that is the most that has been said about it, and this is in accordance with his principle of giving the meaning of oaths a stricter interpretation." Al-Shafi'i said: he fulfils his oath by an hour, unless he has an intention, and this is my view, unless the swearer is an Arab, in which case he is asked: what did you intend? If he explains it with what the word can bear, it is accepted from him, unless it is the lesser meaning. And it follows from Malik's school that it should be understood according to what he explains. And Allah knows best.

This is the answer to the oath. What is meant by "the human being" is the disbeliever, as said by Ibn ʿAbbas in the narration of Abu Salih. Al-Dahhak narrated from him, saying: He means a group of the polytheists: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib ibn Asad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzza, and al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghuth. It was also said: by "the human being" is meant the species of mankind. ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾: in deception (ghabn). Al-Akhfash said: in destruction (halakah). Al-Farra' said: in punishment (ʿuqubah), and from this is the words of the Exalted: ﴿And it was the consequence of its affair loss﴾ [al-Talaq: 9]. Ibn Zayd said: in evil. It was also said: in deficiency; the meaning is close.

It is narrated from Sallam: (wa-l-ʿasri) with a kasra on the ṣad. Al-Aʿraj, Talhah and ʿIsa al-Thaqafi read (khusrin) with a ḍamma on the sin. Harun narrated this from Abu Bakr from ʿAsim. The preferred form in both cases is ittiba' (assimilation of the vowel to the preceding one). It is said: khusr and khusur, like ʿusr and ʿusur. ʿAli used to recite it: ﴿By time, and the calamities of the age, indeed mankind is in loss﴾, and he is in it until the end of the age.

Ibrahim said: Indeed, the human being, when he is granted a long life in this world and becomes senile, is in deficiency, weakness and regression, except the believers, for their rewards for the deeds they used to do in their youth are recorded for them. Its parallel is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿We certainly created man in the best of stature. Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾ [al-Tin: 4-5]. He said: Our recitation is: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, and he is in it until the end of the age﴾. The sound view is what the community and the codices agree upon. The refutation of those who opposed the Mushaf of ʿUthman, and that such readings are not Qur'an to be recited, has already passed in the introduction of this book, so consider it there.

Almighty Allah says: ﴿Except those who have believed﴾. This is an exception from "man" (al-insan), since, according to the sound view, it carries the sense of "people" (al-nas).

Allah says: ﴿and done righteous deeds﴾, meaning they performed the obligatory duties (al-fara'id al-muftaraḍa) incumbent upon them. These were the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: I recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) "By time (al-'Asr)," and then I said: "What is its interpretation, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "Al-'Asr is an oath from Allah; your Lord swears by the end of the day. ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾: Abu Jahl. ﴿Except those who have believed﴾: Abu Bakr. ﴿And done righteous deeds﴾: Umar. ﴿And advised one another to truth﴾: Uthman. ﴿And advised one another to patience﴾: Ali," may Allah be pleased with them all. Similarly, Ibn 'Abbas used to deliver this as a sermon from the pulpit, as a statement attributed to him (mawquf).

The meaning of ﴿wa-tawasaw﴾ is that they loved one another (tahabbu), counselled one another, and urged one another.

﴿Bil-haqq﴾ means "with the Tawhid" (the oneness of Allah). This is what al-Ḍaḥḥak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. Qatadah said: "bil-haqq" means the Qur'an. Al-Suddi said: "al-Haqq" here is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And advised one another to patience﴾ in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and patience in refraining from His disobedience. This has already been mentioned [[see p. 71 of this part.]]. And Allah knows best.
